attempt: Annex says EXTEND works on relative/indexed files; try to find a level or file-organisation condition the OPEN formats omit.
reason: VIII/IX OPEN formats carry EXTEND {file-name-4}; GR11 states the positioning. The unit adds no condition.
quoted: positions the file immediately after the last logical record

attempt: 'released by one or more SEND statements' might add a condition on which messages are purged.
reason: GR1 purges any partial message awaiting transmission to the CD's destinations; same obligation, the SEND clause only describes how such a message arises.
quoted: eliminate any partial message awaiting transmission

attempt: In-line PERFORM might carry a condition beyond the SR/GR (e.g. execution order).
reason: SR1 requires imperative-statement and END-PERFORM when procedure-name omitted; GR3 names it in-line; GR6 gives its execution. Nothing left over.
quoted: is referred to as an in-line PERFORM statement

attempt: TEST BEFORE semantics might not be stated by GR10 or SR3.
reason: GR10c: condition true on entry with TEST BEFORE specified or implied transfers nothing, and TEST AFTER tests after the set; SR3 makes BEFORE the default. Covers both sentences.
quoted: the TEST BEFORE phrase is assumed

attempt: 'At least six AFTER' might differ in scope (VARYING vs format 4) or carry the 1974 limit as an obligation.
reason: SR12 is the same requirement for format 4 (the VARYING format); the two-AFTER sentence is history of the previous standard and obliges nothing.
quoted: At least six AFTER phrases must be permitted

attempt: Variable-length INTO and the NEXT phrase on sequential READ might be permissions no rule states.
reason: GR8b of each READ makes the INTO move a group move for RECORD IS VARYING; VII format carries [NEXT] and GR2 states it is optional. Both sentences covered.
quoted: has no effect on the execution of the READ statement

attempt: NOT AT END of READ might be defined only by the unit.
reason: GR11 of VII.4.4.4 states the actions when the at end condition does not occur, including transfer to imperative-statement-2.
quoted: If an at end condition does not occur during the execution of a READ statement

attempt: NOT INVALID KEY of READ might lack a rule stating its control transfer.
reason: VIII/IX.1.3.5 item 2 (no exception) transfers to the NOT INVALID KEY imperative; READ GR11 applies it. Named ids exist and say it (L2.2 is the list item of GR2 of the invalid key clause).
quoted: control is transferred to the end of the input-output statement

attempt: WITH DATA of RECEIVE might define a condition (data made available) not in GR4.
reason: GR4 transfers control to imperative-statement-2 of WITH DATA when the MCS makes data available in identifier-1; identical.
quoted: the MCS makes data available in the data item referenced by identifier-1

attempt: REPLACE unit might add scope beyond format 1 (format 2 cancel).
reason: Unit states only that matched occurrences are replaced; GR1 states it for format 1; no additional condition.
quoted: Each matched occurrence of pseudo-text-1 in the source program is replaced

attempt: Variable-length RETURN INTO might be a permission with no rule.
reason: XI.4.3.4 GR6b states the size of the current record and the RECORD IS VARYING group move for RETURN INTO.
quoted: If an at end condition does not occur during the execution of a RETURN statement

attempt: NOT AT END of RETURN might carry a condition GR3 omits.
reason: GR3 transfers to imperative-statement-2 when no at end condition occurs, after the INTO move; same obligation.
quoted: If an at end condition does not occur during the execution of a RETURN statement

attempt: Different-length REWRITE in relative/indexed might be a level or organisation condition GR3 omits.
reason: GR3 of VIII.4.6.4 and IX.4.6.4 permits unequal record length in level 2; the unit's (2 REL, 2 INX) is the same scope.
quoted: may or may not be equal to the number of character positions

attempt: NOT INVALID KEY of REWRITE might lack a rule for its transfer.
reason: REWRITE GR10 makes transfer depend on the INVALID KEY / NOT INVALID KEY phrases and points to the invalid key condition rules, whose item 2 states the NOT INVALID KEY transfer.
quoted: depends on the presence or absence of the optional INVALID KEY

attempt: 'New feature' might state that SEND has REPLACING LINE under conditions the rules omit.
reason: SEND format 2 carries [REPLACING LINE]; GR16a states its meaning (and GR17/18 the unsupported-device cases). 'New' is history.
quoted: replace all characters which may have previously been

attempt: Mixed index-name/identifier operands before TO might be a relaxation only the unit states; new variations might lack rules.
reason: Format 1 prints index-name-1 and identifier-1 as alternatives in one repeated group, SR1 applies to all recursions; formats 3 and 4 and GR6/GR7 state the two new variations.
quoted: is placed in the conditional variable according to the rules of the VALUE clause

attempt: Five sentences: relative/indexed USING file and same physical reel might be permissions with no rule.
reason: Format GIVING {file-name-3} ...; SR3/SR10 variable-length sizes; SR8 indexed GIVING and GR12b relative key (GR9 relative USING); SR7 same multiple file reel; GR3 DUPLICATES order. Each sentence has a rule; nothing unmatched.
quoted: The order of the associated input files as specified in the SORT statement

attempt: Row: the permissions on transfers of control and paragraph-name might already be stated by GR7 / IV.4.4.2.
reason: GR7 defines the range only and IV.4.4.2 GR2 the implicit transfer; no numbered rule permits explicit transfers out of or into the procedures. A row stands (SR vs GR is arguable, the paragraph-name sentence is syntax; reader's SR stands, reported not re-decided).
quoted: an implicit transfer of control occurs

attempt: NOT INVALID KEY of START might lack a rule.
reason: START GR7 gives transfer by phrase presence and points to the invalid key condition item 2; same as REWRITE.
quoted: depends on the presence or absence of the optional INVALID KEY

attempt: Row: a rule may already allow a group item as STRING receiver.
reason: SR3 and SR4 restrict identifier-3 (not reference modified, not edited, not JUSTIFIED) and GR4a only says alphanumeric moves; no rule says a group item is permitted. Row stands as the reader's SR.
quoted: must not represent an edited data item

attempt: NOT ON OVERFLOW of STRING might state a condition GR10 omits.
reason: GR10 transfers to imperative-statement-2 when the GR9 overflow conditions are not encountered; same obligation.
quoted: control is transferred to the end of the STRING statement

attempt: SUBTRACT-specific NOT ON SIZE ERROR might need its own rule.
reason: The size error paragraph (VI.6.4.2 p4) states it for every arithmetic statement and SUBTRACT points to it; id exists and says the same.
quoted: the ON SIZE ERROR phrase, if specified, is ignored

attempt: NOT ON OVERFLOW of UNSTRING might carry a condition GR20 omits.
reason: GR20 transfers to imperative-statement-2 when GR17 overflow conditions are not encountered; same.
quoted: control is transferred to the end of the UNSTRING statement

attempt: File-specific USE precedence over open-mode USE might be a priority rule stated only here.
reason: GR4 of each USE module: with file-name-1 explicit no other USE statement applies; same precedence in other words.
quoted: no other USE statement applies to file-name-1

attempt: GLOBAL scope 'any program contained within' might be broader than the precedence rule.
reason: X.5.5.4 GR1b/1c select the GLOBAL declarative of the directly containing then each more inclusive program: all contained programs. Format carries GLOBAL.
quoted: The declarative in which the GLOBAL phrase is specified

attempt: Same attempt for USE BEFORE REPORTING GLOBAL.
reason: X.5.6.4 GR1b/1c state the same selection for the report declarative; format carries GLOBAL.
quoted: The declarative in which the GLOBAL phrase is specified

attempt: NOT END-OF-PAGE of WRITE might carry a condition GR9 omits.
reason: GR9 transfers to imperative-statement-2 when the end-of-page condition does not occur; same.
quoted: the end-of-page condition does not occur

attempt: NOT INVALID KEY of WRITE might lack a rule.
reason: WRITE GR9 gives transfer by phrase presence and points to the invalid key condition item 2; same as REWRITE.
quoted: control is transferred to the end of the input-output statement

attempt: Row: the lead-in might be a pure lead-in or restated, so not a row; or have a different kind.
reason: Ends in a period, 25 words, so no lead-in test; nothing restates it. A definitional row is the conservative disposition and keeps it in the denominator.
quoted: introduced by the Intrinsic Function Amendment

attempt: Function definition might differ (derived automatically vs invoked mechanism) or scope (object program).
reason: A.1.2.1 p1: temporary data item whose value is determined by an implementor mechanism at the time of reference during execution of a statement; same meaning, Amendment 1 applied in this text.
quoted: a function is a temporary data item whose value is determined

attempt: Row: same attempt as p2 for the Correction Amendment list.
reason: Ends in a period, 23 words; no rule restates it; definitional row stands.
quoted: introduced by the Correction Amendment

attempt: Format-1-only claim might differ from GR9 which sits after the FORMAT 1 header.
reason: GR9 (Amendment 2 correction, placed immediately after the FORMAT 1 header) reads 'Identifier-1 is a sending data item', same words, format 1.
quoted: Identifier-1 is a sending data item

attempt: BEFORE/AFTER item longer than one character with REPLACING CHARACTERS might be restricted by SR5 or SR8.
reason: SR5 limits to one character only in level 1 and exempts level 2 (unit is 2 NUC); SR8 restricts only literal-3/identifier-5 for CHARACTERS, not the BEFORE/AFTER item (literal-2/identifier-4). Permission follows from the two rules.
quoted: this restriction on length does not apply to level 2

attempt: Mixture permission for MAX might need a condition the argument rule omits.
reason: Argument rule 1 of MAX: same class except that mixing of alphabetic and alphanumeric is allowed; the unit's permission is that exception, nothing more.
quoted: mixing of arguments of alphabetic and alphanumeric classes is allowed

attempt: Mixture permission for MIN might need a condition the argument rule omits.
reason: Argument rule 1 of MIN: same class except that mixing of alphabetic and alphanumeric is allowed; the unit's permission is that exception, nothing more.
quoted: mixing of arguments of alphabetic and alphanumeric classes is allowed

attempt: Mixture permission for ORD-MAX might need a condition the argument rule omits.
reason: Argument rule 1 of ORD-MAX: same class except that mixing of alphabetic and alphanumeric is allowed; the unit's permission is that exception, nothing more.
quoted: mixing of arguments of alphabetic and alphanumeric classes is allowed

attempt: Mixture permission for ORD-MIN might need a condition the argument rule omits.
reason: Argument rule 1 of ORD-MIN: same class except that mixing of alphabetic and alphanumeric is allowed; the unit's permission is that exception, nothing more.
quoted: mixing of arguments of alphabetic and alphanumeric classes is allowed
